steps.title: Shortcuts that save you hours
steps.body: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+B bold. Know these five by heart and you work twice as fast. On a Mac use Cmd instead of Ctrl.

steps.title: A résumé that looks sharp
steps.body: Use a template (New > search 'resume') or make a simple layout yourself: one font, clear headings via Styles, and no more than one page. Save as a PDF before emailing, otherwise your layout can shift on the recipient's end.

steps.title: Assignments: table of contents, sources, collaboration
steps.body: Use Heading 1/2 and add a table of contents automatically via References > Table of Contents. Manage sources under References > Manage Sources. Working with others on the same file? Save it in OneDrive and share the link so you can type at the same time.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a one-page résumé using a template or your own layout and save it as a PDF.

lessons.title: Excel: budget, formulas and smart filters

steps.title: Your own budget in a sheet
steps.body: Make columns for Date, Description, Category and Amount. With =SUMIF(C:C,"Food",D:D) you add up all spending in one category. That way you see at a glance where your money goes (and why it's always gone).

steps.title: Searching, filtering, conditional formatting
steps.body: Put a filter on your table (Data > Filter). With Home > Conditional Formatting you can, for example, automatically color all amounts over €100 red. With Ctrl+T you turn your range into a real table that grows by itself.

steps.title: Pivot tables and charts
steps.body: A pivot table (Insert > PivotTable) summarizes hundreds of rows in a tidy table: drag 'Category' to Rows and 'Amount' to Values. Add a chart for a presentation or assignment.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a budget sheet with at least ten expenses, add up per category with SUMIF and color amounts over €50 red.

lessons.title: PowerPoint: presentations for school and work

steps.title: Designing without it looking boring
steps.body: Click Design > Designer for automatic suggestions. Little text, big visuals, at most two fonts. Use Insert > Icons for icons instead of clip art.

steps.title: Animations and transitions: less is more
steps.body: One subtle transition (like 'Fade') is enough. Too much flash distracts from your story. Use animations only to make points appear one by one.

steps.title: Collaborating and presenting
steps.body: Share the presentation via OneDrive so your group members can work in it at the same time. Practice with Presenter View (you see notes, the audience doesn't). If you like, ask Copilot or another AI assistant for a first draft, then adapt it to your own story.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a five-slide presentation for a school assignment or internship, using Designer, one chart and no slide with more than six lines.
